mainTopic: Torah study in place of קרבנות, and the final משנה: big or small, what matters is the heart
overview: This amud finishes the story of the altar Jews built in Alexandria, and explains 'עיר ההרס' as the city of the sun, with a proof from איוב. רב הונא explains that the 'sons' in ישעיהו are the settled exiles of בבל and the 'daughters' are the unsettled exiles of other lands. רב teaches that only the nations between צור and קרטיגני recognize ישראל and ה׳. When challenged from מלאכי, he answers that the far-away nations only call Him 'the God of gods'. A series of teachings follows: Torah learning, anywhere and even at night, counts like bringing קרבנות and doing the Temple service, and רבא adds that one who learns Torah does not need קרבנות at all. The last משנה of the מסכת teaches that a big קרבן and a small one are equal, as long as the heart is aimed at Heaven. The גמרא backs this up with פסוקים from קהלת and a ברייתא of בן עזאי showing that ה׳ needs nothing from our offerings. It ends with the rule that a קרבן slaughtered without awareness (מתעסק) is פסול, and closes מסכת מנחות.

steps.title: An altar is built in Alexandria
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the פסוק about the five cities in Egypt and says that Jews went to Alexandria and built a מזבח there for the sake of Heaven, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...and swear to the Lord of hosts.' They went to Alexandria in Egypt, built an altar, and offered sacrifices on it for the sake of Heaven, as it says: 'On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story from the previous page and says that Jews in Egypt built a מזבח in Alexandria. It brings a פסוק that seems to predict this altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'לשם שמים' tells us that their intention was to serve ה׳, not עבודה זרה. The פסוק 'ביום ההוא יהיה מזבח לה׳ בתוך ארץ מצרים' is read as a description of this altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Altar on which קרבנות are offered
For the sake of Heaven, meaning to serve ה׳
They offered up sacrifices
The Lord of hosts, a name of ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: 'לשם שמים' does not mean the altar was allowed. It only tells us that their intention was to serve ה׳ and not idols.

phrases.english: and swear to the Lord of hosts.
phrases.notes: This is the end of ישעיהו 19:18, about five cities in Egypt. The גמרא began quoting it just before this.

phrases.english: They went to Alexandria of Egypt
and built an altar
and offered sacrifices on it for the sake of Heaven,
as it is said: "On that day there will be an altar
to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 19:19

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלְכוּ לַאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם וּבָנוּ מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the altar in Egypt from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jews built a מזבח in Alexandria for the sake of Heaven, as ישעיהו 19:19 describes.

steps.title: What does 'the city of destruction' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the phrase 'עיר ההרס יאמר לאחת' from the same פסוק and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One shall be called the city of destruction.' What does 'one shall be called the city of destruction' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a puzzling phrase in the same פסוק and asks for its meaning. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'הרס' means destruction, which sounds odd in a פסוק praising cities that swear by ה׳. The גמרא wants to know which city this is and why it has that name.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the city of destruction'; the next steps explain it
One of them will be called

phrases.english: "One shall be called the city of destruction,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 19:18. 'One' means one of the five cities.

phrases.english: what does "one shall be called the city of destruction" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to another phrase in the same פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'עיר ההרס'.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the city of the sun
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's Aramaic translation explains that 'עיר ההרס' is בית שמש, the city of the sun, which will one day be destroyed and is one of the five cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translates it: 'The city of בית שמש, which is destined to be destroyed. It was said that it is one of them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב יוסף's Aramaic translation. 'עיר ההרס' is the city of the sun, and it is one of the five cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reads 'הרס' in two ways. It means 'sun,' which gives the name of the city, and it also hints at destruction, since the city will be destroyed. This explains both the name and the harsh-sounding word.

keyTerms.meaning: Translates into Aramaic
City (Aramaic)
Literally 'house of the sun,' the name of the city
Destined to be destroyed

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translates it into Aramaic:
"The city of Beit Shemesh, the city of the sun,
which is destined to be destroyed,"
it was said that it is one of them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the five cities in Egypt from the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'עיר ההרס'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עיר ההרס' is the city of the sun (בית שמש), which will be destroyed, and it is one of the five cities.

steps.title: How do we know 'הרס' means sun?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the word 'הרס' can refer to the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that 'עיר ההרס' is a word for the sun?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of רב יוסף's translation. This sets up the proof from a פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's reading depends on 'הרס' meaning sun. That is not the usual meaning, so the גמרא wants a source in תנ״ך.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Language or term
The sun (Aramaic)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that "city of heres"
is a word for the sun?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּ״עִיר הַהֶרֶס״ לִישָּׁנָא דְּשִׁימְשָׁא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for רב יוסף's translation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that 'הרס' means sun.

steps.title: Proof from איוב: 'חרס' is the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from איוב that 'חרס' means sun, since ה׳ 'commands the חרס and it does not rise.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Who commands the sun (חרס), and it does not rise.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק in which 'חרס' clearly means the sun, because it speaks about something that rises.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the sun 'rises,' so 'חרס' in this פסוק must mean the sun. The גמרא treats 'הרס' (with a ה) and 'חרס' (with a ח) as the same word, and that supports רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: The sun (poetic word in תנ״ך)
Will rise (shine)

steps.whatToRemember: 'עיר ההרס' is the city of the sun, one of the five cities in Egypt. 'חרס' means sun, as in איוב.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Who commands the sun (cheres), and it does not rise."
phrases.notes: איוב 9:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.

steps.title: רב הונא: sons from afar and daughters from the ends of the earth
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that in ישעיהו, the 'sons' are the exiles of בבל, whose minds are settled, and the 'daughters' are the exiles of other lands, whose minds are unsettled.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Bring My sons from afar and My daughters from the end of the earth.' 'Bring My sons from afar': רב הונא said these are the exiles of בבל, whose minds are settled like sons. 'And My daughters from the end of the earth': these are the exiles of other lands, whose minds are not settled, like daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the Jews of Egypt to Jewish communities in other places. רב הונא explains why the פסוק calls some exiles 'sons' and others 'daughters.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not about which exiles are more beloved. It is about how settled their minds are. The exiles in בבל are calm and stable, like sons, and the exiles elsewhere are unsettled, like daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: Exiled Jewish communities
Babylonia
Their minds are settled and calm
Other countries

phrases.english: "Bring My sons from afar and My daughters from the end of the earth":
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 43:6

phrases.english: "Bring My sons from afar":
Rav Huna said:
These are the exiles of Babylonia,
whose minds are settled, like sons.
"And My daughters from the end of the earth":
These are the exiles of other countries,
whose minds are not settled, like daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the Jewish community in Egypt to Jewish communities in other lands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'sons' are the settled exiles of בבל, and the 'daughters' are the unsettled exiles of other lands.

steps.title: From צור to קרטיגני the nations recognize ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the nations from צור to קרטיגני recognize ישראל and their Father in Heaven, while the nations beyond that region do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב חסדא, and some say in the name of רב יהודה, in the name of רב: from צור until קרטיגני, people recognize ישראל and their Father in Heaven. But from צור toward the west and from קרטיגני toward the east, they recognize neither ישראל nor their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רב, passed down through a chain of rabbis, about the region where the nations know the Jewish people and ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'ואמרי לה' shows that there are two versions of who passed this teaching on from רב. The teaching contrasts two areas: one region knows ישראל and ה׳, and the lands beyond it do not.

keyTerms.meaning: They recognize or know
Their Father in Heaven, meaning ה׳
Toward the west
Carthage, a city in North Africa

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר רַב יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא,

phrases.english: and some say that Rav Yehuda said, that Rav said:
From Tyre until Carthage

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the Jewish people scattered among the nations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nations between צור and קרטיגני recognize ישראל and ה׳, and those beyond that region do not.

steps.title: A verse suggests that ה׳'s name is great everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא challenges רב using a פסוק in מלאכי that says ה׳'s name is great among the nations from east to west.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא challenged רב: 'From the rising of the sun until it sets, My name is great among the nations, and in every place offerings are presented to My name, and a pure מנחה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא is attacking רב's teaching from the step before, which said the far-away nations do not recognize ה׳. He brings a פסוק that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said only the nations from צור to קרטיגני recognize ה׳. The פסוק says ה׳'s name is great 'from sunrise to sunset', which means the whole world. So it looks like even the far-away nations know Him.

keyTerms.meaning: From where the sun rises until where it sets, meaning the whole world
Among the nations
Burned as an offering
Brought close or presented as an offering

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya raised an objection to Rav:
phrases.notes: He's challenging what רב said just before, about the nations from צור to קרטיגני.

phrases.english: "From the rising of the sun until it sets,
phrases.notes: מלאכי 1:11

phrases.english: My name is great among the nations;
and in every place offerings are burned and presented to My name,
and a pure meal offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's teaching that the nations beyond צור and קרטיגני do not recognize ה׳.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says ה׳'s name is great among the nations across the whole world, from east to west, so even the far-away nations seem to recognize Him.

steps.title: They call Him the God of gods
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the nations only call ה׳ 'the God of gods' while still worshipping idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: 'שימי, is it you asking this?! The פסוק means that they call Him the God of gods.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge. He says the פסוק does not mean the far nations truly serve ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nations admit that ה׳ is the highest power, the 'God of gods.' But they still serve their idols under Him. So 'My name is great' means they respect His name, not that they recognize Him as the only God. That fits with what רב said before.

keyTerms.meaning: The God of gods, the highest power over all other powers
That they call Him

phrases.english: He said to him: Shimi, is it you?!
It means that they call Him the God of gods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means all nations truly recognize and serve ה׳.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nations only call Him 'God of gods' while still worshipping idols, so רב's teaching stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The far-away nations admit ה׳ is the highest power, but they still serve idols. This is not real recognition.

steps.title: Can offerings really be brought in every place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק can say offerings are brought to ה׳ 'in every place', since offerings may only be brought in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'In every place offerings are burned and presented to My name.' Could you really think offerings may be brought in every place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at another part of the same פסוק and asks a question on it. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offerings may only be brought in the one place ה׳ chose, the בית המקדש. So the words 'in every place' cannot be read literally. The גמרא needs a new way to understand them.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (meaning: that cannot be right)
In every place

phrases.english: "In every place offerings are burned and presented to My name" —
Would it enter your mind that this means in every place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a phrase from the פסוק quoted in step 8 and asks about its meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'in every place offerings are brought' mean, if offerings may only be brought in the בית המקדש?

steps.title: Torah scholars learning anywhere count as bringing offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that the פסוק refers to תלמידי חכמים who learn Torah everywhere, and ה׳ counts it as if they brought offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: These are תלמידי חכמים who learn Torah in every place. ה׳ says: I count it for them as if they burn and present offerings to My name.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question of the last step. The 'offerings in every place' are really Torah learning, which can happen anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real offerings can only be brought in one place, but Torah can be learned anywhere. ה׳ gives the learners credit as if they brought offerings. So the פסוק is about Torah study, not actual קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah scholars
I count it for them, I give them credit
As if

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says that Rabbi Yonatan says:
These are Torah scholars

I count it for them
phrases.notes: ה׳ is the one speaking here, as in the פסוק.

phrases.english: as though they burn and present offerings to My name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'In every place' means תלמידי חכמים learning Torah anywhere, which ה׳ counts as bringing offerings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the main idea of the rest of the section: Torah study can take the place of the קרבנות.

steps.title: A pure מנחה is learning Torah in purity
steps.stepSummary: The end of the פסוק, 'a pure מנחה', refers to someone who learns Torah in purity: he marries first and then learns.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a pure מנחה': this is someone who learns Torah in purity. He marries a woman and afterwards learns Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining the same פסוק. Now it explains the words 'a pure מנחה' in the same Torah-study way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Torah study is like an offering, then 'a pure מנחה' is Torah learned in purity. The גמרא defines this as someone who marries first and then learns. That way his learning is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A pure meal offering
In purity
Marries a woman

phrases.english: "And a pure meal offering" —
this is one who studies Torah in purity:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה וְאַחַר כָּךְ לוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: he marries a woman and afterward studies Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק as step 11, now the words 'a pure מנחה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning Torah in purity means marrying first and then learning.

steps.title: What does 'at night' mean in the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in תהלים about ה׳'s servants who stand in His house 'at night' and asks what 'at night' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A Song of Ascents: Behold, bless ה׳, all servants of ה׳, who stand in the House of ה׳ at night.' What does 'at night' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק that praises Torah scholars. It asks a question here to set up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Temple service is done during the day, not at night. So it is strange that the פסוק talks about servants standing in the בית המקדש at night. The גמרא wants to know who these night servants are.

keyTerms.meaning: A Song of Ascents, the heading of some chapters in תהלים
Servants of ה׳
At night

phrases.english: "A Song of Ascents: Behold, bless the Lord,
phrases.notes: תהלים 134:1

phrases.english: all you servants of the Lord,
who stand in the House of the Lord at night."
What is the meaning of "at night"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second פסוק with the same theme as step 11: Torah study in place of the Temple service.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who are the servants of ה׳ standing in the בית המקדש at night, if there is no service at night?

steps.title: Learning Torah at night counts as the Temple service
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the 'night servants' are תלמידי חכמים who learn Torah at night, and the פסוק counts it as if they did the Temple service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: These are תלמידי חכמים who learn Torah at night. The פסוק counts it for them as if they were busy with the Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question of the last step. The people 'standing in ה׳'s house at night' are those who learn Torah at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No real service happens at night, so the פסוק must mean something else. רבי יוחנן says it means night-time Torah learning. The פסוק gives these learners credit as if they did the עבודה in the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The service in the בית המקדש
The פסוק, the written verse

steps.whatToRemember: Both teachings say the same idea: Torah learning, anywhere and even at night, is counted by ה׳ like the offerings and service of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'At night' refers to תלמידי חכמים who learn Torah at night, which counts as doing the Temple service.

steps.title: An altar in Heaven where Michael brings offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב explains that 'forever' in the פסוק refers to an altar in Heaven, where the angel מיכאל brings קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is forever for Israel.' רב גידל said in the name of רב: this is a built altar, and מיכאל the great prince stands and brings a קרבן on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק that says the Temple service is 'forever.' רב explains how that can be true even after the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה said the service would last forever, but the בית המקדש was later destroyed. רב answers that the service never stopped: an altar still stands in Heaven, and מיכאל brings קרבנות on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A built altar, here meaning the altar in Heaven
The great prince, a title for the angel מיכאל
An offering brought on the altar

phrases.english: "This is forever for Israel"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב ב:ג. שלמה is speaking about the service in the בית המקדש, which was later destroyed. So how can it be 'forever'?

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
This is a built altar,
phrases.notes: He means an altar in Heaven, which stays standing even after the earthly בית המקדש is gone.

phrases.english: and Michael, the great prince,
stands and offers a sacrifice on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם זֹאת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of פסוקים about the Temple service continuing in some form, with a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Forever' refers to the altar in Heaven, where מיכאל keeps bringing קרבנות.

steps.title: Scholars learning the laws of the service are like building the Temple
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the same פסוק differently. It refers to תלמידי חכמים who learn the laws of the עבודה, and ה׳ counts it as if the בית המקדש were built in their days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: these are תלמידי חכמים who are busy with the laws of the Temple service. The פסוק counts it for them as if the בית המקדש had been built in their days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second explanation of 'forever' that is about people learning, not about Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the service continues in Heaven. For רבי יוחנן, it continues on earth through learning: studying the laws of the עבודה is counted as if the בית המקדש were standing. This matches what רבי יוחנן said in Step 14 about learning at night.

keyTerms.meaning: The laws of the Temple service
The פסוק counts it for them (gives them credit as if)
The בית המקדש, the Holy Temple

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the idea that learning the laws of קרבנות today stands in for the actual service.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
These are Torah scholars
who are busy with the laws of the Temple service,
the verse credits them
as if the Temple were built in their days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק that רב explained in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning the laws of the עבודה is counted as if the בית המקדש were built in one's days.

steps.title: Learning Torah is like bringing every kind of offering
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads 'זאת התורה לעולה למנחה ולחטאת ולאשם' as teaching that anyone who learns Torah is considered to have brought all these קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does the פסוק mean, 'This is the Torah of the עולה, of the מנחה, of the חטאת, and of the אשם'? Anyone who learns Torah is as if he brought an עולה, a מנחה, a חטאת, and an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a new פסוק and reads the word 'Torah' in it as Torah learning in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק simply sums up the laws of the different קרבנות. ריש לקיש reads it as 'Torah learning goes together with the עולה, the מנחה' and so on. So learning is counted as if you brought each of these.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is busy learning Torah
A burnt offering, burned completely on the altar
A meal offering made of flour
A sin offering
A guilt offering

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
What is meant by what is written:
"This is the Torah of the burnt offering, of the meal offering,
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:לז

phrases.english: and of the sin offering, and of the guilt offering"?
Anyone who is busy with Torah

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיב עוֹלָה, מִנְחָה, חַטָּאת, וְאָשָׁם.
phrases.english: is as if he offered a burnt offering, a meal offering, a sin offering, and a guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching on the same theme with a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning Torah is counted as if one brought an עולה, a מנחה, a חטאת and an אשם.

steps.title: רבא questions the wording behind ריש לקיש's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: if the פסוק meant 'as if he brought them,' it should have said 'עולה ומנחה,' not 'לעולה למנחה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This 'לעולה למנחה' (for the עולה, for the מנחה)? It should have said 'עולה ומנחה' (an עולה and a מנחה)!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges ריש לקיש's reading by pointing to the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If learning is like actually bringing the קרבנות, the פסוק should simply list them: 'עולה ומנחה.' Instead, each one starts with the letter ל ('for the עולה'). So רבא says ריש לקיש's reading does not fit the words. This sets up רבא's own reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For the עולה, for the מנחה', each word starting with ל
It should have said

phrases.english: Rava said:
This "for the burnt offering, for the meal offering"?
It should have said "a burnt offering and a meal offering"!
phrases.notes: רבא is bothered by the extra ל ('for the') in front of each קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's reading from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading that learning is as if one brought the קרבנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'לעולה למנחה' does not fit 'as if he brought an עולה and a מנחה'. For that meaning the פסוק should have said 'עולה ומנחה'.

steps.title: רבא: one who learns Torah does not need offerings at all
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own reading: someone who learns Torah does not need an עולה, חטאת, מנחה or אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Anyone who learns Torah does not need an עולה, nor a חטאת, nor a מנחה, nor an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces ריש לקיש's reading with his own, which fits the wording 'for the עולה, for the מנחה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the פסוק as 'Torah does the job of the עולה, of the מנחה,' and so on. So it is not just that learning is like bringing a קרבן. Learning means the person no longer needs to bring one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introducing a new explanation in place of the old one
Does not need

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: learning Torah is AS IF you brought every קרבן. רבא: because of the wording 'לעולה', he reads it as: one who learns Torah does not NEED the קרבנות at all.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying Torah learning is worth less than קרבנות. He is saying it goes further: learning takes the place of the קרבן entirely.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Anyone who is busy with Torah
does not need a burnt offering,
(nor a sin offering,) nor a meal offering,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some leave them out.

phrases.english: nor a guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own objection by giving a new reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reading with one that fits the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning Torah is as if one brought each קרבן (ריש לקיש).
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the ל in 'לעולה', the פסוק means one who learns Torah does not need these קרבנות at all.

steps.title: Learning the laws of a חטאת or אשם is like bringing one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads the פסוקים 'זאת תורת החטאת' and 'זאת תורת האשם' as teaching that whoever learns the laws of each קרבן is considered as if he brought that קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Why does the Torah say 'This is the law of the sin offering' and 'This is the law of the guilt offering'? To teach that whoever learns the law of the sin offering is like someone who brought a sin offering. And whoever learns the law of the guilt offering is like someone who brought a guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds another teaching to the series about Torah learning and קרבנות. He says that learning the laws of a specific קרבן counts as if you brought that קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק focuses on the word 'תורת', the law of each קרבן. His teaching is more specific than ריש לקיש's in Step 17: learning the laws of a חטאת counts as bringing a חטאת, and learning the laws of an אשם counts as bringing an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the sin offering
Busy with, learning
As if he brought (the קרבן)
Guilt offering

steps.whatToRemember: After the בית המקדש, learning the laws of a קרבן takes the place of bringing it: learning about a חטאת is like bringing a חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a main source for the custom of learning the laws of the קרבנות, as a way of 'bringing' them when there is no בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the meaning of what is written, "This is the law of the sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:18

phrases.english: and "This is the law of the guilt offering"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:1

phrases.english: Anyone who learns the law of the sin offering
is as if he brought a sin offering,
and anyone who learns the law of the guilt offering
is as if he brought a guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further teaching about Torah learning in place of קרבנות, after רבא's reading in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning the laws of a חטאת or אשם counts as if one brought that קרבן.

steps.title: Big or small offering, what matters is the heart
steps.stepSummary: The משנה notes that 'אשה ריח ניחוח' is said about an animal עולה, a bird עולה, and a מנחה. This teaches that giving much and giving little are equal, as long as the intention is for Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For an animal burnt offering the Torah says 'a fire offering, a pleasing aroma.' For a bird burnt offering it says 'a fire offering, a pleasing aroma.' And for a flour offering it says 'a fire offering, a pleasing aroma.' This tells you that the one who gives a lot and the one who gives a little are the same, as long as he directs his heart to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, the last one in מסכת מנחות. It teaches that a cheap קרבן is just as pleasing to ה׳ as an expensive one, if it is brought with the right heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal costs the most, a bird costs less, and a מנחה of flour costs the least. Yet the Torah uses the exact same words, 'אשה ריח ניחוח', for all three. So what makes a קרבן pleasing is the person's heart, not the price. The condition is that the person directs his heart to Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: An עולה brought from an animal
An עולה brought from a bird
A fire offering, a pleasing aroma (to ה׳)
The one who gives much and the one who gives little
That he directs his heart toward Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: A little with the right heart is equal to a lot: 'אחד המרבה ואחד הממעיט, ובלבד שיכוין לבו לשמים'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is used far beyond קרבנות. It is often quoted about Torah learning, צדקה, and every kind of עבודת ה׳.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
It is said about an animal burnt offering
"A fire offering, a pleasing aroma,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:9

phrases.english: and about a bird burnt offering, "A fire offering, a pleasing aroma,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:17

phrases.english: and about a flour offering, "A fire offering, a pleasing aroma,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:2

phrases.english: to tell you:
the one who gives much and the one who gives little are the same,
as long as he directs his heart toward Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. The Torah learning discussion ends here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A big קרבן and a small קרבן are equally pleasing to ה׳, as long as the person's heart is directed to Heaven.

steps.title: רבי זירא's source: the sweet sleep of the worker
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a פסוק from קהלת as the source for the משנה: 'Sweet is the sleep of the worker, whether he eats little or much.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי זירא said: What is the verse that teaches this? "Sweet is the sleep of the worker, whether he eats little or much."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks for a פסוק that supports the משנה's idea. רבי זירא finds one in קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'worker' (עובד) is read as a person who serves ה׳ by bringing a קרבן. 'Whether little or much' matches the משנה's 'המרבה והממעיט'. Either way, his 'sleep is sweet', meaning he can be calm that his קרבן is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (that teaches this)?
Sweet
The worker; here, one who serves ה׳

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Zeira said: What is the verse?
"Sweet is the sleep of the worker,
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:11. The גמרא reads 'worker' as someone serving ה׳ with a קרבן.

phrases.english: whether he eats little or much."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק as the source for the משנה's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that a big and a small קרבן are equal
steps.raayaSupportSource: קהלת 5:11, 'מתוקה שנת העבד אם מעט ואם הרבה יאכל'

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה's source: more food, more eaters
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה brings a different פסוק from קהלת: 'When good things increase, those who eat them increase, and what advantage is there to its owner?'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: The source is from here: "When good things increase, those who eat them increase, and what advantage is there to its owner?"
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers a different פסוק as the source for the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bigger קרבן just means more כהנים eat from it. It does not give the owner extra merit. What counts is what ה׳ 'sees', meaning the owner's true intention.

keyTerms.meaning: From here (introduces a different source)
Advantage, benefit
Owner (here, the one who brings the קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים from קהלת back up the משנה: רבי זירא's 'מתוקה שנת העבד' and רב אדא בר אהבה's 'ברבות הטובה רבו אוכליה'. Both teach that the size of the gift does not matter, only the heart.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: From here:
"When good things increase, those who eat them increase,
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:10. A bigger קרבן just means more כהנים get to eat from it.

phrases.english: and what advantage is there to its owner?"

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק from רבי זירא's as the source for the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that a big and a small קרבן are equal
steps.raayaSupportSource: קהלת 5:10, 'ברבות הטובה רבו אוכליה ומה כשרון לבעליו'

steps.title: Only the name of ה׳ appears in the sections about offerings
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי notes that the קרבנות sections use only the name ה׳, never אל or אלהים, so no one can argue that different offerings go to different gods.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן עזאי says, look at the sections about קרבנות. The names 'אל' and 'אלהים' are never used there, only 'ה׳'. This is so that an opponent will have no opening to argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which בן עזאי points out which name of ה׳ the Torah uses when it talks about קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah used different names of ה׳ for different קרבנות, a heretic could claim that each קרבן goes to a different power. By using only one name, ה׳, the Torah closes that door. This sets up the next part of the same ברייתא, about 'אשה ריח ניחוח לה׳'.

keyTerms.meaning: The sections of the Torah that deal with offerings
Literally 'an opening of the mouth', meaning an excuse or a chance to make a claim
An opponent in an argument; here, someone who wants to argue against the Torah
Other names of ה׳ that are not used in the קרבנות sections

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי:
phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה מָה כְּתִיב בְּפָרָשַׁת קׇרְבָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: Come and see what is written in the section of offerings,
that neither 'El' nor 'Elokim' is said in them,
but only 'ה׳',
so as not to give an opening
to an opponent to argue.
phrases.notes: He means someone who would claim that different offerings are brought to different gods.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פסוקים from קהלת supporting the משנה's idea, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that develops the theme of 'ריח ניחוח לה׳'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרבנות sections use only the name ה׳, so no one can claim that the offerings are brought to different powers.

steps.title: A big bull, a small bird and a flour offering are all called a pleasing aroma
steps.stepSummary: The same words 'אשה ריח ניחוח' are used for a large bull, a small bird and a מנחה, which teaches that a big gift and a small gift are equal if the heart is aimed at Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says 'אשה ריח ניחוח' about a big bull, about a small bird, and about a מנחה. This teaches you that the one who gives a lot and the one who gives a little are the same, as long as he aims his heart toward Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי continues and shows the source for the idea from the משנה (step 21): the Torah uses the same praise for every size of קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bull costs a lot, a bird costs little, and a מנחה of flour costs even less. Yet the Torah uses the exact same words, 'אשה ריח ניחוח', for all of them. So what counts to ה׳ is the person's intention, not the size of the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A big, heavy bull, an expensive offering
A small, thin bird, a cheap offering
'A fire offering, a pleasing aroma', the Torah's phrase of acceptance for a קרבן
The one who gives a lot and the one who gives a little are equal
That he aims his heart toward Heaven, meaning he does it for the sake of ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: The value of a קרבן to ה׳ depends on the heart behind it, not on how expensive it is.

phrases.english: And it is said about a big bull: 'A fire offering, a pleasing aroma',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:9

phrases.english: and about a small bird: 'A fire offering, a pleasing aroma',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:17

phrases.english: and about a flour offering: 'A fire offering, a pleasing aroma',

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לְךָ: אֶחָד הַמַּרְבֶּה וְאֶחָד הַמַּמְעִיט,
phrases.english: to tell you: the one who gives a lot and the one who gives a little are the same,
as long as he aims his heart toward Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of בן עזאי, moving from the name ה׳ to the phrase 'אשה ריח ניחוח'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the same words of acceptance are used for big and small offerings, giving much and giving little are equal when the intention is for Heaven.

steps.title: Maybe ה׳ needs the offerings as food
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי raises a possible wrong idea: perhaps ה׳ needs the קרבנות to eat, so a bigger offering would be better.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you would say that He needs it for eating,
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible objection that it is about to answer. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ריח ניחוח', pleasing aroma, could make someone think that ה׳ enjoys the קרבן like food. If so, a big bull would clearly be better than a small bird, which would go against what was just taught. The ברייתא raises this thought so it can knock it down.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And in case you would say', a way of raising a possible mistaken idea
He needs it for eating

phrases.english: And in case you would say: He needs it for eating,
phrases.notes: 'He' means ה׳. If that were true, a bigger offering would be better, so the ברייתא has to reject it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible challenge to the idea from step 25 that big and small offerings are equal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that a big offering and a small offering are equal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ה׳ needed the offering as food, a bigger offering would give Him more, so the big one would be worth more.

steps.title: Verses from תהלים show ה׳ does not need food
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with פסוקים from תהלים: the whole world belongs to ה׳, and He does not eat meat or drink blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'If I were hungry I would not tell you, for the world and everything in it is Mine.' And it says: 'For every animal of the forest is Mine, the cattle on a thousand hills. I know every bird of the mountains, and the creatures of the field are with Me.' And: 'Do I eat the meat of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the wrong idea from step 26 by quoting פסוקים from תהלים that show ה׳ needs nothing from us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything in the world already belongs to ה׳, so He has no need for our animals. The last פסוק says it openly: ה׳ does not eat meat or drink blood. So the size of the קרבן cannot matter because of any need of His.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches', the source that answers the question
The world and everything in it
The creatures that move in the field
Mighty ones; here, strong bulls
Goats

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם אֶרְעַב לֹא אֹמַר לָךְ
phrases.english: The פסוק teaches: 'If I were hungry I would not tell you,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 50:12

phrases.english: 'for the world and everything in it is Mine',
And it says: 'For every animal of the forest is Mine,'
'the cattle on a thousand hills;'
'I know every bird of the mountains,'
'and the creatures of the field are with Me',
'Do I eat the meat of bulls,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 50:13. It is a question that expects the answer 'of course not'.

phrases.english: 'or drink the blood of goats?'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם אֶרְעַב לֹא אֹמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possible objection of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from פסוקים that the premise of the objection is false
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think ה׳ needs the offerings as food, so bigger is better.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything belongs to ה׳ and He does not eat or drink, so He needs nothing from the offerings.

steps.title: Offerings are brought for our own good, not for ה׳'s needs
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ did not command קרבנות as a trade, 'I do His will and He does mine'. We bring them for our own benefit, as the פסוק says 'לרצנכם תזבחהו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: I did not tell you to bring offerings so that you would say, 'I will do His will and He will do my will.' You are not bringing offerings for My will; you are bringing them for your own will, as it says: 'You shall offer it for your own acceptance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with its main message: קרבנות are not a deal with ה׳, they are for the benefit of the person who brings them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ה׳ needs nothing (step 27), a person cannot think he is doing ה׳ a favor and can expect a favor back. The פסוק 'לרצנכם תזבחהו' shows the קרבן is for the person's own sake, so that he will be accepted and forgiven. This fits the idea that a small gift with a good heart is as good as a big one.

keyTerms.meaning: Offer sacrifices
'I will do His will and He will do my will', the wrong idea of a trade with ה׳
'You shall offer it for your own acceptance', meaning for your own benefit

steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ does not need קרבנות at all. They are given to help us, so what matters is the heart we bring with them, not their size.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לרצונכם' does not mean 'whenever you feel like it'. It means the קרבן is for your own good, so that you will be accepted before ה׳.

phrases.english: I did not tell you, 'Offer sacrifices',
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is speaking in the voice of ה׳ here.

phrases.english: so that you would say, 'I will do His will and He will do my will.'
You are not offering for My will,
rather, you are offering for your own will,
as it says: 'You shall offer it for your own acceptance.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 27: since ה׳ needs nothing, קרבנות must be for the person's own benefit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קרבנות are not a trade with ה׳. They are for the good of the one who brings them, so a small offering given for Heaven is as worthy as a large one.

steps.title: A second reading: sacrifice with awareness
steps.stepSummary: The words 'לרצנכם תזבחהו' are read in a new way: slaughter the קרבן knowingly, on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'לרצנכם תזבחהו' means slaughter with your will, slaughter with your awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second meaning to the same פסוק it just used. Now it means you must slaughter the קרבן with awareness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 28, 'לרצנכם' meant 'for your benefit.' Here it means 'with your will and knowledge.' This turns a lesson about attitude into a rule about how the slaughter must be done.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; a second way to read the same words
With your will (earlier read as 'for your benefit')
With your awareness; knowingly

phrases.english: Another explanation:
'You shall sacrifice it lirtzonchem':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:5. This is the same פסוק from the last step, now read a new way.

phrases.english: slaughter with your will,
slaughter with your awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the פסוק cited in Step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן must be slaughtered knowingly and on purpose.

steps.title: שמואל asks: where do we learn that a מתעסק disqualifies a קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: To back up the new reading, the גמרא brings a question שמואל asked רב הונא about slaughtering without intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As שמואל asked רב הונא: from where do we know that if someone handles קדשים without intending to, the קרבן is פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a conversation that shows where the reading in Step 29 comes from. It opens with a question about a person who slaughters without meaning to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק is someone whose action happens without purpose, for example he meant to do something else and ended up cutting the animal's throat. שמואל wants the source in the תורה that such a slaughter disqualifies the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we learn this)? A request for a source
Someone who does an act without intending to do it
Holy offerings, קרבנות
Disqualified; not valid

phrases.english: As שמואל asked רב הונא:
From where do we know, regarding one who acts unawares with holy offerings,
that it is disqualified?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל מֵרַב הוּנָא מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the case that the reading in Step 29 is based on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that slaughter by a מתעסק disqualifies a קרבן.

steps.title: First answer: slaughter for the sake of a bull
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא cites 'ושחט את בן הבקר': the slaughter must be done knowingly, for the sake of the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'And he shall slaughter the young bull.' The slaughter must be for the sake of a young bull.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his first source. The פסוק describes slaughtering 'the bull,' so the person must know he is slaughtering the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes slaughtering the bull, so the slaughter has to be done knowingly, aimed at the animal. A מתעסק has no such aim, so his slaughter does not match the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughter of the animal
For the sake of; with intention toward
A young bull

phrases.english: As it says: 'And he shall slaughter the young bull,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5

phrases.english: meaning the slaughter must be for the sake of a young bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ושחט את בן הבקר' requires the slaughter to be done with the bull in mind.

steps.title: שמואל pushes back: that does not show it is essential
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the bull פסוק only shows the proper way. It does not show that without intent the קרבן is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We already know this. But where do we learn that it is essential?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל is not satisfied with the answer. He wants a source that shows the קרבן is ruined without intent, not just that intent is the right way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק can show the ideal way to do a מצוה without saying that missing it ruins the act. שמואל accepts the first point but asks for a source that makes it לעכב, essential.

keyTerms.meaning: In our hands; something we already know
To hold back; essential, so that without it the act is invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל rejects the bull פסוק. He agrees it teaches the right way. He is only asking where we learn that missing it disqualifies the קרבן.

phrases.english: He said to him: This we already have in hand,
but from where do we learn that it is essential?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the answer in Step 31 goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'ושחט את בן הבקר.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That פסוק shows the proper way to slaughter, but not that slaughter without intent is invalid.

steps.title: 'לרצנכם' makes awareness essential
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers with 'לרצנכם תזבחהו': slaughter with awareness. This makes intent essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'לרצנכם תזבחהו,' slaughter with your awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings a second פסוק that proves awareness is essential. This is the reading the גמרא gave in Step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads 'לרצנכם תזבחהו' as 'לדעתכם זבחו', slaughter with your awareness. This פסוק is taken as the source that awareness is essential (לעכב), not just the proper way. So a מתעסק's slaughter is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces a source from the תורה
Slaughter (an order to the listeners)

steps.whatToRemember: A קרבן slaughtered without awareness (מתעסק) is פסול. 'ושחט את בן הבקר' shows the right way, and 'לרצנכם תזבחהו' makes it essential.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה that a קרבן needs a purposeful act of slaughter. An accidental cut is not enough.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'You shall sacrifice it lirtzonchem':
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא talking now, answering שמואל.

phrases.english: slaughter with your awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's challenge from Step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Intent might only be the proper way, based on 'ושחט את בן הבקר.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לרצנכם תזבחהו' makes awareness essential, so a מתעסק's slaughter is פסול.

steps.title: הדרן: closing the chapter הרי עלי עשרון and מסכת מנחות
steps.stepSummary: The closing words for the last chapter, הרי עלי עשרון, and for the whole of מסכת מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הרי עלי עשרון, and מסכת מנחות is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the discussion. It is the traditional closing words said when we finish a chapter, and here the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הדרן עלך' expresses the hope to come back and learn this chapter again. 'סליקא לה' says that the מסכת is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said when finishing a chapter
Is finished; is complete
A tractate of the תלמוד

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'הרי עלי עשרון,'
phrases.notes: That's the name of the chapter we just finished, taken from its opening words.

phrases.english: and Tractate מנחות is completed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter and the מסכת after the last discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter הרי עלי עשרון and all of מסכת מנחות are complete.
